summary: Mount Arab's steel Aermotor lookout, built 1918 in St. Lawrence County NY; the last of seven county towers, restored by volunteers, open to the public.

facts.design: Prefabricated steel Aermotor tower with a 7 x 7 ft metal cab, built by the Aermotor Corporation; an observer's cabin stands across from it
facts.agency: NY Dept. of Environmental Conservation, with the volunteer Friends of Mount Arab

staffing.status: Summer summit stewards hired by Friends of Mount Arab; the cabin museum opens when one is on duty

access.note: Open to the public; the tower can be climbed. The observer's cabin museum opens when a summit steward is on duty, late spring to early fall.

visit.trail_note: About a two-mile round-trip hike to the summit; the Friends of Mount Arab group maintains the trail.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR and Adirondack Explorer give 35 ft (about 10.7 m); Wikipedia gives 40 ft (12 m). The record uses 10.7 m from the two sources that give the tower's own dimension; the Wikipedia figure is unverified.
1911 is the wooden predecessor tower and the start of fire observation on the mountain; 1918 is the steel Aermotor tower now standing.

sources.title: History of Arab Mountain - Beyond the Fire Tower

notes_for_editor: Height conflict (35 ft vs 40 ft) is unresolved; the NRHP nomination PDF (Haynes and Garofalini, 2000) is not digitized on NPGallery, so it could not settle it. Adirondack Explorer carries an old COVID-19 editor's note saying the towers are closed; not used, so current access rests on the NHLR and Explorer text. NHLR gives the lookout elevation as 2,519 ft; Explorer gives the peak as 2,539 ft (not in facts). No notable fires are named in any source read. Friends of Mount Arab's history page returned 404 in the cache.
